title: Stream API: Partial payload persistence, telemetry enhancements, and customer escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several high-value Hosted API customers reported truncated streaming responses and repeated partial payloads after transient network disconnects. Root cause appears to be a race between the server-side flush/close path and our streaming session checkpointing; in some cases the session metadata was not atomically persisted before the final send, leading clients to reconnect and receive overlapping partials or missing final tokens. This ticket scopes an immediate mitigation, telemetry to characterize incidence, and a playbook for customer escalation and long-term fix.

Impact: High — customer-facing transcript corruption and duplicate segments in production for both small and long token sessions. Affects Hosted primarily but we need config guidance for Dedicated and Private where checkpoint persistence and operator settings differ.

Goals: 1) Ship a rollback-safe immediate mitigation to reduce customer-visible partials. 2) Add fine-grained telemetry and per-session checksums to measure incidence and enable forensics. 3) Deliver a robust server-side atomic checkpoint + client resume handshake change in runtime-1.22 to fully eliminate races. 4) Publish an escalation playbook and customer communication templates.

Repro steps (internal):
- Create long streaming generation (>1024 tokens) with forced small batch sizes.
- Inject short TCP disconnect during finalization (simulate gateway restart).
- Observe session metadata sometimes not persisted; client reconnects request resume token and server either returns overlapping content or replays up to last persisted checkpoint.

Hypothesis / Root cause:
- In the final flush path we perform two async operations: persist session checkpoint to Redis and stream final bytes to the connection. Under timing skew the connection final write completes and the connection is torn down before the persist completes; the reconnection logic uses a resume token generated before persist, creating duplicate/transient partials.

Immediate mitigations (hotfix - targeted for runtime-1.21.3):
- Change finalization to prefer strong ordering: await session checkpoint persist with a soft timeout (200ms) before returning terminal event to SSE clients.
- Emit a final "finalized_marker" event with both sequence and a short SHA1 checksum of the last N bytes so clients can detect duplicate tail fragments.
- Increase server-side ephemeral session retention from 30s -> 60s for hosted gateway to give more time for backend persist during brief gateway restarts.
- Add a transparent client SDK patch that treats identical final checksums as idempotent and suppresses duplicate terminal tokens.

Telemetry / Observability additions:
- New metric: stream.partial_repair_rate (by model, route, region).
- Per-session tags: resume_token_hash, last_persist_latency_ms, final_write_latency_ms.
- Tracing spans for checkpoint.persist and sse.stream_final with correlation_id set to request_id.
- Dashboard: streaming-integrity -> shows percent of sessions with checksum mismatch, grouped by customer and model.

Long-term fix (runtime-1.22):
- Introduce an atomic checkpoint API: server receives final write acknowledgement before advancing resume epoch. Use consensus-backed persist (write-through to Redis + object-store checkpoint for very long sessions).
- Update client handshake: resume token now includes epoch + checksum; on reconnect client provides last-seen checksum, server validates and returns repair instructions or a deterministic replay window.
- Add end-to-end e2e tests in CI that fuzz network flaps and assert no duplicate tail fragments for 10k simulated sessions.

Dedicated / Private considerations:
- Dedicated operators may have lower Redis durability; document configuration: enable checkpoint_write_policy=write_through and session_retention_override=60s in the dedicated YAML.
- Private deployments on air-gapped networks must apply a CLI schema migration to enable atomic_checkpoint API; provide upgrade notes in release.

Customer comms & escalation playbook:
- Triage step: Confirm customer session ids and retrieve streaming-integrity traces within 24h.
- Immediate action: enable hosted mitigation per-customer (soft timeout + checksum) and verify with synthetic replay in staging.
- Communication template: apologize, describe mitigation applied, offer a 30-day credits package and a postmortem once runtime-1.22 ships.
- Escalation timeline: 0-6h: acknowledgement and debug request; 6-24h: mitigation applied or customer on a hotfix branch; 24-72h: rollback-safe fix deployed to hosted and rollout plan for dedicated/private customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- runtime-1.21.3 mitigation deployed to canary customers with visible drop in stream.partial_repair_rate by >80% in canary population.
- Telemetry and dashboard deployed and ingested for top 20 customers.
- runtime-1.22 long-term fix merged with e2e network-flap tests passing in CI and documented upgrade notes for Dedicated/Private.
